title: QBR facilitator cheat-sheet and renewal scorecard (draft)
content:
Purpose: Practical one-page facilitator reference for running a focused 60–75 minute QBR that surfaces health signals, aligns on renewal risk, and leaves with clear next steps. Includes a lightweight renewal scorecard and an attachable post-meeting action ledger for AEs and SEs.

Audience: CSM (lead facilitator), assigned AE, Solutions Engineer (optional), customer stakeholders (product, eng, ops).

Before the meeting (CSM checklist)
- Confirm attendees and roles (ask AE to confirm exec presence if renewal < 90 days)
- Update renewal date and current contract value in CRM (example fields: renewal_date, ARR, committed_models)
- Prepare 2–3 usage slides: latency P50/P95, token spend trend (30/90 days), feature usage (embeddings vs chat vs reranking)
- Run the renewal scorecard quick assessment (see below) and add a 1–2 line pre-read summary
- Share agenda and pre-reads 3 business days in advance; ask for 10-minute pre-meeting input: top 2 priorities, any blockers
- Tech prep: test screen share, ensure SE has sample prompt traces if relevant

Suggested meeting agenda (60 minutes)
- 0:00–0:05 — Quick intros & objective: "Today is about what went well, where we have friction, and what we need to do to make next quarter successful and ensure renewal is on track."
- 0:05–0:15 — Business outcomes review (customer exec): wins, priorities, any org changes
- 0:15–0:25 — Health & performance snapshot (CSM presents metrics; call out any regressions or incidents)
- 0:25–0:40 — Value deep-dive (SE + CSM): example deployments, cost/latency tradeoffs, proposed tuning or model variants to hit targets
- 0:40–0:50 — Risk & opportunity review (use scorecard to guide discussion)
- 0:50–0:60 — Commitments and next steps (owner + due date for each). If renewal < 60 days, schedule executive alignment follow-up within 7 days.
- Optional 60–75 min — Technical breakout with engineering team (if live debugging or architecture changes needed)

Facilitator script snippets (concise language to keep the meeting on track)
- Kickoff: "Thanks everyone — to be respectful of time, we'll keep this tight and leave with 3 concrete owners and dates."
- When a blocker appears: "That's a critical point. For the remainder of this meeting let's capture it as an action with an owner and then if needed we'll arrange a follow-up deep dive — who should own that?"
- When exec signals low priority: "Understood — can you share what other priorities are consuming cycles so we can map impact and timing?"
- Closing: "Recap: three commitments — owner, deliverable, due date. We'll share minutes within 24 hours and add follow-ups to the renewal ledger."

Renewal scorecard (quick scalar rubric, 0–3 per line, guidance in parentheses)
- Usage trend (3=steady growth or healthy plateau; 2=flat; 1=declining; 0=sporadic/unused)
- Value alignment (3=clear ROI & roadmap fit; 2=some ROI; 1=unclear; 0=no alignment)
- Technical reliability (3=no incidents; 2=minor incidents; 1=periodic regressions; 0=frequent outages)
- Cost predictability (3=within budget and predictable; 2=some spikes; 1=major surprises; 0=customer-facing billing disputes)
- Exec sponsorship (3=active exec champion; 2=engaged manager; 1=low exec interest; 0=no exec visibility)
- Contract runway (3=>9 months; 2=6–9 months; 1=3–6 months; 0=<3 months)
- Total possible: 18. Scoring guidance: 14–18=green, 9–13=yellow (engage AE), 0–8=red (escalate to CS lead + AE immediately)

Sample quick tracker template (text table you can paste into CRM/notes)
| Customer | Renewal | Score | Top risk | Next step | Owner | Due date |
| Acme Co | 2026-08-15 | 11 (yellow) | Cost spikes on embeddings | Run quantization pilot + cost projection | SE Jordan | 2026-03-22 |

Post-meeting action ledger (owner-friendly checklist)
- Create follow-up email with minutes and scorecard summary — Owner: CSM, Due: +1 business day
- Open a technical spike ticket for proposed tuning (attach prompt traces) — Owner: SE, Due: +7 days
- Schedule executive alignment if scorecard in yellow/red — Owner: AE, Due: +7 days
- Update CRM renewal probability and linked opportunities — Owner: CSM, Due: +2 days
- Add proposed configuration change to onboarding/work-items board if accepted — Owner: Product Ops, Due: next sprint planning

Escalation playbook (when scorecard = red)
- Immediate steps: AE intro to customer exec within 48 hours; CS lead to schedule weekly touchpoints; open incident-style internal thread with SRE/SE if issue is reliability related
- Template subject line for AE intro: "Redwood/QBR follow-up: immediate exec sync re: renewal risks" (body: include scorecard, top 3 risks, proposed mitigations)

Notes on facilitation dynamics and staffing
- Who leads: CSM owns agenda and minutes; AE owns commercial commitments; SE owns technical follow-ups. For small customers, CSM may own AE tasks until handoff.
- If renewal < 3 months, invite a Sales Engineer and CS lead to reduce friction for urgent escalations.

Retention interventions examples you can propose live
- Short-term: throttling policy and token budget alerts, model variant to reduce cost by X%, caching of frequent prompts
- Mid-term: dedicated capacity trial (cost+SLA) or a quantization pilot with estimated cost delta
- Contract: pilot extension tied to predefined success metrics (latency, cost per 1M tokens, uptime)

Template follow-up email (one-paragraph)
"Thanks for your time today. Attached are the QBR minutes and the renewal scorecard. High level: scorecard = [GREEN/YELLOW/RED], top 3 actions are [bulleted]. Owner/due dates included. If you'd like an exec sync, please let us know availability next week."

Appendix: tips and common pitfalls
- Pitfall: too much internal detail — keep the business lens up front (execs care about outcomes and risk).
- Tip: use the scorecard live in the meeting — numerical anchors reduce ambiguity about "how risky" renewal is.
- Tip: embed a recorded 3-minute usage demo if you plan customer-by-customer product suggestions.

Open questions for iteration
- Do we want the scorecard weights to be configurable per segment? (SMB vs mid-market vs enterprise)
- Should we attach a standardized one-slide ROI worksheet per customer?
- Can we automate scorecard population from telemetry in the console?

-- End of draft.

Editors: please flag anything that would overlap with existing CS playbooks and suggest how we might surface the scorecard in Salesforce or our internal QBR template for auto-population.
